ayahs.1: Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened to the Qur'an and said to their fellows, 'We have heard a recitation that amazes us.'
ayahs.2: It guides to what is right, so we believed in it, and we will never commit shirk—giving anything the devotion owed to Allah alone.
ayahs.3: We believe our Rabb—Exalted is His Majesty—has taken neither a mate nor offspring.
ayahs.4: The foolish among us used to speak outrageous falsehoods about Allah.
ayahs.5: We had assumed that humans and jinn would never fabricate lies about Allah.
ayahs.6: Some men used to seek refuge with jinn, and that only pushed both sides deeper into wrongdoing.
ayahs.7: Those humans thought, as you jinn did, that Allah would never resurrect anyone for judgment.
ayahs.8: We used to try to reach the heavens for news, but found them guarded by stern angels and shooting stars.
ayahs.9: We used to take positions there to eavesdrop, but whoever tries that now finds a blazing flare waiting.
ayahs.10: We no longer know whether harm is intended for those on earth, or whether their Rabb intends good for them.
ayahs.11: Among us are the righteous and the less so—we have always been divided into factions.
ayahs.12: We now know we cannot outwit Allah on earth, nor escape Him into the heavens.
ayahs.13: When we heard the guidance, we believed in it. Whoever trusts their Rabb need not fear their reward being cut short or being wronged.
ayahs.14: Among us are those who submitted to Allah and those who deviated. Those who submitted have found the Straight Path.
ayahs.15: As for the deviant, they will be fuel for Hell.'
ayahs.16: If those who reject the truth had followed the Straight Path, We would have granted them abundant rain to drink—
ayahs.17: as a test. Whoever turns away from the dhikr—the conscious remembrance—of their Rabb will be driven into crushing punishment.
ayahs.18: Places of worship belong to Allah alone; do not call upon anyone besides Him.
ayahs.19: Yet when Allah's servant stood calling on Him alone, the pagans almost swarmed over him.
ayahs.20: Say: I call only upon my Rabb, associating none with Him in worship.
ayahs.21: Say: I have no power to harm or benefit you.
ayahs.22: Say: No one can protect me if I disobey Allah, nor can I find refuge except with Him.
ayahs.23: My duty is only to convey what comes from Allah and deliver His messages. Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger will be in the Fire of Hell forever.
ayahs.24: Only when they see what they were warned about will they know who had weaker allies and fewer supporters.
ayahs.25: Say: I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Rabb has set it far off.
ayahs.26: He is the Knower of the unseen and discloses none of it to anyone—
ayahs.27: except to messengers He chooses. Then He posts angel-guards before and behind them
ayahs.28: so that the messengers fully deliver their Rabb's messages—though He already knows everything about them, and keeps precise account of all things.
